§2.2 Never Drop, Never Invent

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

principles-never-drop-never-invent · principles

✅ Normative

Every piece of printed content MUST survive into the output (never drop), and the output MUST NOT contain a label, value, span, header, structure or relationship that the page does not print (never invent).

Almost every rule in this protocol exists to prevent one of these two failures.

Never drop

Printed content means visually perceptible content under The Page Is the Ground Truth§2.1. Hidden, microscopic or imperceptibly low-contrast source strings are outside that scope; visible but unreadable text is retained as evidence with [illegible], not silently discarded.

A visible row, column, cell, marker, header, caption, footnote, stamp or repeated table MUST appear in the output. The most-dropped items are the last row of a table, trailing summary lines, detached cells beside a grid, sparse columns proven only by their header, and text in the margins.

Where the protocol is unsure how to represent something, the rendering that loses no content is the conforming one.

Never invent

The output MUST NOT add what the page does not print. A rowspan is a claim that the page merged those cells; if the page printed them separately, the claim is false. A heading level, a header tier, a list nesting or a table boundary is likewise a claim about the page and MUST be supported by it.

Placeholders that stand for content — [image], [The image shows…], ... — are invented and MUST NOT appear, except the explicit markers this protocol defines (such as [blank] for an empty form field and [signature]).
